concepts.title: Three Passions Governed a Life
concepts.definition: Bertrand Russell opens with supreme simplicity: three passions, simple but overwhelmingly strong, have governed his life -- the longing for love, the search for knowledge, and pity for the suffering of mankind. Like great winds, they blew him this way and that over a wayward course across a deep ocean of anguish to the very verge of despair.
concepts.key_idea: Three winds, one life -- love, knowledge and pity blew Russell across seas of anguish to despair's edge and back.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww132.txt opening (three passions simple but overwhelmingly strong, longing for love, search for knowledge, pity for suffering mankind, great winds, wayward course, ocean of anguish)
question_patterns: name the three passions that governed bertrand russell's life

solution_steps.explain: Love, knowledge and pity -- named in one breath as the governing winds of his life.
The winds-and-ocean metaphor makes the passions forces of weather, not choices of taste.
The same winds drove him near despair -- passion, Russell admits, is not comfort.

concepts.title: Love First, Knowledge Second
concepts.definition: Russell sought love first because it brings ecstasy -- an ecstasy so great he would sacrifice all the rest of life for a few hours of it; it relieves loneliness, the terrible loneliness in which the consciousness of the world stands beyond a fearful abyss; and it unites the solitary vision of saints and poets in a glimpse of the heaven sages and poets have imagined. With equal passion he sought knowledge -- the hearts of men, why stars shine, and the Pythagorean power by which number holds sway above the flux.
concepts.key_idea: Ecstasy, antidote to loneliness, glimpse of heaven -- then the hearts of men and the stars: love leads, knowledge follows.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww132.txt love and knowledge sections (ecstasy, terrible loneliness, fearful abyss, glimpse of heaven, hearts of men, why stars shine, pythagorean power, number holds sway above the flux)

solution_steps.explain: Ecstasy, relief from loneliness, and a foretaste of heaven -- love's three answers to Russell's longing.
Knowledge of human hearts, of the stars' shining, of number's rule over change -- equal in force to love.
Love warms, knowledge lights -- Russell refuses to rank one above the other in his life's arithmetic.

concepts.title: Pity, and a Life That Has Been Worth Living
concepts.definition: Pity for the suffering of mankind carried Russell back up: children in famine, victims tortured by oppressors, helpless old people a hated burden, loneliness, poverty and pain -- the whole mockery of what life should be. He longs to alleviate the evil, and he too suffers; yet he would live the life again, for at last he has found it worth living.
concepts.key_idea: Pity returns him to the human sea -- and having carried all three winds, he would live it all again.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww132.txt pity and conclusion sections (children in famine, victims tortured by oppressors, helpless old people hated burden, loneliness poverty pain, would live my life again, worth living)

solution_steps.explain: Famine, torture, the hated burden of the old, loneliness, poverty and pain -- the echo of a world's cry reaches him.

solution_steps.action: state the wish and the limits
solution_steps.explain: He would alleviate the evil, but he too suffers -- pity's power is sympathy, not cure.
Despite the anguish, the three passions make his life worth living -- the essay's final, earned affirmation.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Give Russell's three reasons for seeking love, in his order.

solution_template.explain: Love brings ecstasy -- bliss so great he would trade all the rest of life for hours of it.
Love relieves loneliness -- the terrible isolation from which the world seems a fearful abyss.
Love unites one in a glimpse of the heaven that saints and poets have imagined -- the best that life can offer.

worked_examples.question_pattern: How does pity stand in tension with Russell's first two passions?

solution_template.explain: Love and knowledge lift him -- ecstasy and understanding carry him upward.
Pity drags him back to famine, torture and lonely old age -- the world's anguish returns him to earth.
His life oscillates between heaven's glimpse and earth's cry -- and that is exactly why he calls it worth living.
